articles.headline: OFAC Designates Indian and Turkish Entities, Issues Iran-Related Alert and Amends Venezuela GL
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations targeting entities and individuals in India and Turkey. This action is part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' aimed at disrupting Iran's ability to fund its activities through oil sales.

Among the designated entities are Alexarya Finserv Private Limited, Aryavart Ship Management Private Limited, Oceaniek Technologies India, and Viharaboating Private Limited, all based in India. Individuals Ashwani Kumar Dhiman and Ishwinder Singh, also from India, were designated for their association with Aryavart Ship Management Private Limited.

Additionally, Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services Inc was designated for providing ground handling and other services to several U.S.-sanctioned Iranian airlines. OFAC also published an Iran-related Alert titled 'Iranian Shadow Fleet Reliance on False Flags for Sanctions Evasion' and issued Venezuela-related General License 5AA, authorizing certain transactions related to the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5 Percent Bond on or after December 18, 2026.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License for International Development Bank for Investment and Finance
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Iran General License FF-1, which authorizes the wind down of transactions involving the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance. This amended general license replaces and supersedes the previous General License FF.

The updated license permits the wind-down of transactions with the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance, also known as Iraq Development Bank, and certain majority-owned entities through December 1, 2026.
A key provision of the amended license requires that any payments to blocked persons must be made into blocked accounts.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates North Korea-Linked IT Workers and Rwandan Entities for DRC Support
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations targeting North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. These actions aim to counter illicit activities supporting North Korea's weapons programs and Rwanda's backing of the M23 movement in eastern DRC.

For North Korea, OFAC sanctioned ten individuals and one entity involved in government-run IT worker schemes. These schemes reportedly use fraudulent identities to secure employment with U.S. businesses, generating revenue that supports North Korea's weapons development.

In relation to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, OFAC sanctioned the Rwandan Ministry of Defence and Zigama Credit and Savings Society, a Rwandan financial institution. These designations were made for their alleged role in facilitating Rwanda's support for the March 23 Movement (M23) and its political wing in eastern DRC.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks Settles with OFAC for $1.5 Million Over Russia Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based cloud networking solutions provider, has agreed to pay $1,529,685 to settle nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations. The violations stemmed from exports of networking equipment and services to a Russian defense manufacturer that was blocked by operation of law.

Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme exported equipment and services to Joint Stock Company Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian missile and air defense manufacturer. MMZA was majority-owned by JSC Concern Almaz-Antey, a designated Russian state-owned company, making MMZA a blocked person at all relevant times, even though it was not explicitly listed on the SDN List until June 2022.

OFAC determined that the apparent violations were egregious but voluntarily self-disclosed. The settlement emphasizes the importance of thorough sanctions-related due diligence, especially when acquiring companies or assets, and maintaining vigilant oversight of foreign operations.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Reporting Requirements
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has amended 11 of its Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) concerning blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC. This update is part of an ongoing review to ensure published guidance remains current.

The revised FAQs, numbered 10, 32 through 36, 41, 42, 49, 50, and 53, clarify when financial institutions must freeze funds due to a blocked person's interest versus rejecting a prohibited transaction where no blockable interest exists. They also address reporting procedures, including the 10-business-day deadline for reporting blocked property and rejected transactions.

Key changes include updated guidance on the interest required on blocked funds, permissible service charges, notification to customers, and the distinction between a customer inquiry and an actual payment instruction. All reports for blocked property and rejected transactions must now be submitted through the OFAC Reporting System (ORS).

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Removes Belarus and North Korea Listings, and Releases New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations, alongside the removal of certain entities from its Belarus and North Korea sanctions lists. The agency also issued new general licenses related to Iran and Russia, and amended existing Frequently Asked Questions.

The Iran-related designations target corporate service providers, shipping agents, and vessels allegedly involved in Iranian commodities networks. This action underscores OFAC's continued focus on disrupting illicit financial and maritime activities supporting the Iranian regime.

In addition to the designations, OFAC issued Iran General Licenses GG and HH, authorizing wind-down activities, limited safety and environmental transactions, and the offloading of cargo involving certain blocked persons or vessels. General Licenses were also issued for Russia-related transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements PAIPA Designations and Issues Associated General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA), adding new entities to its Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions List. These designations carry explicit banking, foreign-exchange, lending, and investment restrictions.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC issued PAIPA General License 1, 'Transactions Authorized Pursuant to the Cyber-Related Sanctions Regulations,' and PAIPA General License 2, 'Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving Certain Entities Blocked on October 19, 2026.' General License 2 provides a time-limited wind-down authorization until January 19, 2027.

The new listings include Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Phase I Venture Capital Center Limited Partnership (a.k.a. Miracle Plus RMB Fund I), a Chinese entity. This action highlights the U.S. government's commitment to protecting American intellectual property and countering cyber-related threats.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Venezuela-Related General License for Earthquake Relief
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Venezuela-related General License 60A, titled 'Authorizing Transactions Related to Earthquake Relief Efforts in Venezuela.' This amended general license aims to facilitate humanitarian assistance in the region.
In addition to the new general license, OFAC also issued an amended Frequently Asked Question, FAQ 1263, providing further guidance on Venezuela-related sanctions.

This action follows previous Venezuela-related General Licenses issued by OFAC, which have included reporting requirements for transactions related to purchases and investments in Venezuela's natural resource sectors.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian Entities and Cuban Bank, Issues New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations and a Cuba designation, alongside the issuance of new and amended general licenses and Frequently Asked Questions.

The State Department designated Cuba's BANCO INTERNACIONAL DE COMERCIO S.A. (BICSA) pursuant to E.O. 14404, for providing services to the designated Iran's International Development Bank for Investment and Finance.

OFAC also issued an Iran-related general license covering the wind-down of transactions involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance. Additionally, two Russia-related general licenses were issued, authorizing certain transactions involving Lukoil retail service stations outside Russia and certain Lukoil entities in Bulgaria.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuelan National Assembly President Jorge Rodríguez from Sanctions List
body: The U.S. Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced the removal of Jorge Jesús Rodríguez Gómez, president of Venezuela's National Assembly, from its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List. This delisting covers five separate entries associated with Rodríguez.

Rodríguez had been designated under Executive Order 13692 in September 2018. His removal signifies a strategic shift in U.S. policy towards Venezuela, moving from punitive economic containment to structured access and engagement with the Venezuelan regime.

While the removal restores his access to the U.S. financial system, it does not lift all restrictions. Canada still lists him under its Venezuela regulations, and a separate U.S. visa restriction reportedly remains in place.

articles.headline: UK Sanctions List Corrects Entry for Zenith Global Corporation Limited
body: On November 3, 2026, the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) updated the UK Sanctions List on GOV.UK with a correction to the entry for Zenith Global Corporation Limited. This administrative amendment clarifies existing information related to the entity.

The correction involves deleted information appearing in strikethrough and red, with newly added information underlined and highlighted in yellow. Zenith Global Corporation Limited remains subject to asset freeze, trust services sanctions, director disqualification sanction, and transport sanctions.

Transport sanctions prohibit ships and aircraft owned, controlled, chartered, or operated by a designated person from entering or overflying the UK, respectively. They also include a prohibition on technical assistance relating to such aircraft and ships.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Pays $1,529,685 to OFAC for Russia Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based artificial intelligence and cloud networking solutions provider, has agreed to pay $1,529,685 to settle its potential civil liability for nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme exported networking equipment and related services from the United States to Joint Stock Company Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian defense manufacturer. MMZA was majority-owned by a designated Russian state-owned company, making it a blocked person.

OFAC determined that Extreme's apparent violations were egregious and voluntarily self-disclosed. This action highlights the importance of robust sanctions-related due diligence, especially concerning acquired entities and oversight of foreign operations.

articles.headline: BIS Streamlines Export Controls for Sound Suppressors, Transfers to EAR
body: The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has announced that, as of November 20, 2026, the export of certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors will be subject to BIS's Export Administration Regulations (EAR). This deregulatory action transfers control from the State Department's U.S. Munitions List.

This change aligns export controls on suppressors with those already applied to firearms. Under the new rule, suppressors will be added to the Commerce Control List (CCL), and a BIS license will be required for certain exports, reexports, or in-country transfers, including releases of related software and technology to foreign persons.

Jeffrey I. Kessler, Under Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Security, stated that this move alleviates compliance burdens on the firearms industry while continuing to protect national security. License exceptions currently available for firearms will also be applicable to suppressors.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
